correctness.rationale: The reset coin sequence determines the two-state part chain. Uniform destinations of genuine cross-part steps are independent coupon streams, with stationary step rates gamma/(1+gamma) into B and gamma^2/(1+gamma) into A, both count variances O(t). At t=s_n(log n+x), random count errors are o_P(n), so the joint exact conditional coupon coverage formula gives independent Poisson missing-count limits with means e^{-x} and gamma exp(lambda/gamma)e^{-x}. This proves the Gumbel and last-class laws. Exact rational finite-state independent-recursion assertions passed; they do not replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary articles on position-reset walks, resetting cover times, memory-reset self-avoiding walks, and broad Gumbel search limits. None of their stated results supplies the fixed-r growing-biclique two-intensity Gumbel law and n/log n last-side crossover. Semantic research-record and prior-claim comparisons revealed no implication-equivalent record. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment; general heterogeneous Markov-modulated collection theorems remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: Root resetting breaks alternation by adding returns to an already visited root, creating unequal genuine coupon arrival rates. Their competition moves the bottleneck threshold from equal class sizes to ratio 1-r, with an n/log n perturbation creating an explicit logistic last-covered-side transition. This is a naturally motivated structural fluctuation result for exhaustive search, not a parameter substitution or known-table evaluation.
